subject.title: Feature Request: Session rotation/archive lifecycle event for cron job triggers

question: Should OpenClaw expose session archive/rotation as a cron-matchable durable lifecycle event, or route this use case through the existing plugin session_end lifecycle boundary?
rationale: Current main has pieces of the workflow, but the requested cron event contract would add public scheduling/config semantics and security-sensitive autonomous agent turns that automation should not choose without maintainer intent.

options.title: Approve Narrow Event Trigger
options.body: Add an additive event schedule or equivalent lifecycle trigger with durable event_id, scoped session metadata, explicit permissions, trace records, docs, and tests across archive/rotation paths.

options.title: Bless Plugin session_end
options.body: Document session_end plus plugin-owned workflow scheduling as the supported extension point and close or narrow this core cron-trigger request if that path covers the use case.

options.title: Fold Into Related Hook Design
options.body: Keep this issue linked to the internal session-end and cron-hooks design items until maintainers choose one lifecycle API boundary for all of them.

recommendation.title: Approve Narrow Event Trigger
recommendation.body: Add an additive event schedule or equivalent lifecycle trigger with durable event_id, scoped session metadata, explicit permissions, trace records, docs, and tests across archive/rotation paths.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision spans cron schemas/runtime plus the security model for unattended automation, where steipete has the strongest current routing history among the likely owners.
